# ETF Premium and Discount

⚠️ **Trading warning / Avertissement trading** : informational only, not investment advice. A premium or a discount is a measurement with context, not by itself a reason to buy or sell an ETF. Curated by Skill Harbor: an ETF premium and discount workbench built on a simple question with a complicated answer, namely whether the market price matches the value of what the fund holds. The snapshot route computes the premium or discount to NAV for one ETF and immediately compares it with same-category peers, because a 1 percent premium means one thing on a large US equity fund and something quite normal on a crypto or leveraged fund; category interpretation bands are built in. Comparison and screener routes rank many ETFs from deepest discount to highest premium across a common universe organized by category (bonds, international, commodities, leveraged and inverse, derivative income, crypto). The deep-dive route explains why a gap exists: demand surges, time-zone mismatch, creation bottlenecks, stale NAV, or futures contango. The most advanced route decomposes a sudden large move into a NAV-driven part and an excess-premium part, estimates dealer gamma exposure from the options chain, and lays out a convergence timeline across hours, days, and weeks. Data comes from Yahoo Finance through the free yfinance library. From the himself65/finance-skills repository (MIT).
